newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp CEO satisfied with merger solution.
newsitem.headline: Krupp CEO satisfied with merger solution.

text.p: Krupp AG chief executive Gerhard Cromme on Friday conceded that the German engineering firm had not achieved its original goal to take over rival Thyssen AG but said the merger solution had solved problems in the steel industry.
"The original goal was not achieved but it still resolved the steel problem in the shortest possible time," Cromme told a news conference.
Cromme also said that the restructuring costs required to build the new steel business with Thyssen would not be borne by the two parent companies, but by the merged steel company itself.
"The synergies in the next few years should cover restructuring costs. We expect that this will take place over the next three to four years," Cromme said.
He also said both Krupp and Thyssen could be happy with their decision to merge their steel activities, which was approved on Thursday by Thyssen's supervisory board.
"The result of the negotiations .. was attractive enough so we could not turn it down," he said.
Despite the failure of Krupp's original hostile takeover bid for Thyssen, Cromme also said the Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp group did not rule out takeover bids in the future.
"We will not baulk in the future to return to the path we took in other cases, if we are convinced this is right," Cromme said.
Thyssen and Krupp have agreed to merge their activities as of April 1 into a venture 60 percent owned by Thyssen, creating Europe's largest steel firm.
On Thursday, Thyssen chief executive Dieter Vogel said Krupp group would bear all the restructuring costs from the venture.
Thyssen Krupp Stahl will have sales of 11 billion marks and output of 15 million tonnes a year.
